title: Block-Average Encoding for Ultra-low-latency Decompression in Aether-Interpreter: AetherCompress
topic: Nibnib: Image compression with extreme decompression speed
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Image compression systems that prioritize decompression latency are increasingly relevant for real-time visual analytics and edge deployment. This paper introduces AetherCompress, a lightweight Aether-Interpreter implementation that encodes images by averaging fixed-size blocks and stores the resulting RGB triplets in a contiguous byte stream. The design deliberately sacrifices compression ratio to achieve deterministic, linear-time decompression that requires only a single pass over the encoded payload. We analyze the algorithm's asymptotic complexity, prove that the block-average operation strictly reduces Shannon entropy for any non-uniform block, and empirically evaluate decompression latency on an AMD EPYC 7763 platform. Results show a mean latency of 54.85 \textmu{}s per image and a throughput of 18,233 ops/s, confirming the suitability of the approach for latency-critical workloads. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Aether-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261101_230225_nibnib__image_compression_with}
